what_its_for: This medicine helps your heart pump blood more effectively. It is used to treat severe heart failure when your heart is not pumping well enough to meet your body's needs. It works by relaxing the blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, and it helps your heart beat more strongly.
how_to_take: This medicine is given directly into your vein (intravenously, or IV) through a needle or catheter. It is always given by a nurse or doctor in a hospital or clinical setting. You will not give this medicine to yourself at home in most cases. The medicine is already mixed in a solution and flows into your vein slowly and continuously over a period of time set by your doctor. Do not try to adjust the flow rate or touch the IV equipment yourself.
dosing: Your doctor will decide exactly how much medicine you need based on your weight, kidney function, and how your heart is responding to treatment. The dose is carefully calculated and adjusted by your medical team. A typical starting dose is low and may be slowly increased if needed. Blood tests and heart monitoring will be done regularly to make sure you are getting the right amount.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given continuously by medical staff in a hospital, a missed dose is very unlikely. If your IV line becomes blocked, disconnected, or the infusion is stopped for any reason, tell your nurse or doctor right away so they can correct it as quickly as possible.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home. The hospital or clinic handles storage. For reference, the premixed solution should be kept at room temperature, away from direct light, and should never be frozen. Once the bag is connected and in use, the medical team will follow specific guidelines for how long it can safely be used.
what_to_avoid: Tell your medical team about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting this medicine. Avoid getting up too quickly from lying down, as this medicine can lower your blood pressure and cause dizziness. Do not drink alcohol during treatment. Avoid any strenuous activity unless your doctor says it is safe. Do not allow anyone to adjust or disconnect your IV line except your nurse or doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Tell your nurse or doctor right away if you experience any of the following: irregular or fast heartbeat, chest pain or chest tightness, sudden dizziness or feeling faint, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath that gets worse, swelling in your legs or ankles that gets worse, severe headache, numbness or tingling, signs of low blood pressure such as weakness or blurred vision, or any pain, redness, or swelling at the IV site. These could be signs of a serious problem that needs immediate attention.
when_it_works: This medicine begins working fairly quickly, often within minutes of starting the IV infusion. Most patients notice some improvement in breathing and comfort within a few hours. Your medical team will monitor your heart function closely to track how well the medicine is working for you. The full benefit is usually seen during the course of your hospital stay.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially lower blood pressure and irregular heartbeats, so the dose may be adjusted carefully. People with kidney problems may need a lower dose because this medicine is removed from the body mainly by the kidneys. This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless absolutely necessary, and your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits carefully. It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk, so nursing mothers should talk to their doctor before use. Safety in children has not been fully established, and dosing in children is determined carefully by a specialist.
